name: Anti-establishment
summary: Anti-establishment politics opposes a society's conventional ruling institutions and principles, casting the political, economic and cultural elite as corrupt and out of touch with ordinary people. It is a stance rather than a program, used by 1960s counterculture and the New Left, by Occupy and the Seattle protesters, and in the 2010s mostly by right-wing populists. Its positions on the economy, culture and immigration come from whatever ideology it is attached to.
scope: The shared core across strands: elite corruption, hostility to established institutions and experts, and preference for direct popular decision-making, drawn from the 1892 Omaha Platform, Wikipedia's account of anti-establishment views, and Cas Mudde's definition of populism. It does not take a single left or right strand, so most economic and social answers are neutral and low-confidence.

furtherReading.title: Populism (Wikipedia)

furtherReading.title: Mudde: Populism is based on morals

sources.title: Anti-establishment
sources.author: Wikipedia

sources.title: Omaha Platform

sources.usedFor: Primary anti-establishment program: corruption of legislatures, public ownership of railroads, direct election and initiative and referendum.

sources.title: Populism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Ideational definition (people versus elite), views on direct democracy, experts, courts and media, left and right variants.

sources.title: Mudde: Populism is based on morals (interview)
sources.author: International Centre for Defence and Security (ICDS)
sources.usedFor: Cas Mudde on the moral people-versus-elite divide, acceptance of popular sovereignty and attachment to host ideologies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Left strands favor it and right strands dispute it; opposition to the establishment itself implies no healthcare position.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Left-wing anti-establishment movements such as Occupy would say yes, right-wing ones are mixed, so the stance does not settle it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Anti-elite critics attack both state officials and finance, so no side is implied.

public-ownership.rationale: The Omaha Platform wanted public railroads and telegraphs, but modern right-wing anti-establishment parties do not, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Occupy-style left strands say yes and right strands are mixed; the Omaha Platform's graduated income tax is one precedent.

unions-good.rationale: Left strands side with unions; right-wing populists often court workers but distrust union leadership as an establishment.

property-fundamental.rationale: No defining position; the strands differ on property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations count as part of the establishment for the left, while right strands target government and media more, so the answer splits.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare policy comes from the host ideology, not the anti-establishment stance.

worker-ownership.rationale: A left-strand idea absent from the right-wing strand.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Distrust of those in power makes state surveillance suspect, though right-wing strands may accept security measures; inferred from the stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: 1960s counterculture opposed harsh drug laws, while 2010s right-wing strands do not share that view.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anti-establishment movements tend to resist speech limits imposed by official norms; inferred, and left strands may differ.

strong-leader.rationale: Populist leaders claim to speak directly for the people and bypass intermediary institutions and gridlock; inferred and contested on the left.

state-harmful.rationale: Anti-establishment views oppose those who hold power, not the state as such; only anarchist strands say it is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Strands split: American right-wing strands oppose limits, left strands may favor them.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and military are establishment institutions, but right-wing strands support them; adherents split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A social question without a stance-based answer.

decide-locally.rationale: Populists contrast the people with distant elites, so moving decisions closer to citizens fits; inferred rather than a stated plank.

rehabilitation.rationale: Host-dependent: left strands favor it, right strands punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Social conservatism is a host-ideology matter; 1960s counterculture rejected conventional norms while 2010s right-wing strands defend them.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: 1960s liberation strands supported gay rights, while many right-wing strands oppose; adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not defined by the stance; religion is part of the establishment for some and of the people for others.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: 1960s strands opposed racial inequality, but right-wing strands now reject such policies as establishment orthodoxy.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Right-wing strands see this as a progressive establishment norm, left strands may accept it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Right-wing strands stress it and left strands do not; no stance-based answer.

gradual-change.rationale: Anti-establishment views are defined by opposition to established principles and institutions, so respect for them is rejected.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Right-wing populists want it, left strands do not; the Omaha Platform opposed 'undesirable' immigration but this is not the core.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are seen as remote elites by both Seattle-era and right-wing critics; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The 1999 Seattle WTO protests were anti-establishment from the left and tariffs appeal to right strands too, so no consistent answer.

nation-first.rationale: Right strands say yes and left strands reject it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-war 1960s strands said no, but the stance does not decide it.

open-borders.rationale: Not part of the stance and rejected by right-wing strands.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Right strands treat climate policy as elite agenda, left strands demand action; split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Some strands (1968 radicals) accept it, but most contemporary populist movements work through elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populism treats the people's common sense as superior to elite expertise, and the stance opposes the institutions that experts staff.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Host-dependent; left strands favor it, right strands do not.

basic-income.rationale: Left strands such as Occupy might back it, while right-wing strands tend to resist; the stance gives no answer.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Appeals to some populist strands but is not a defining plank.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Omaha Platform's 'plain people' framing fits small owners, but modern strands differ.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not part of the stance; only radical left strands.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Distrust of finance runs through the stance (Occupy, Omaha money plank), but other strands want central bank control of money.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anti-establishment movements oppose entrenched ruling groups; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; hereditary rule is an establishment in the literal sense but few adherents address it.

democracy-best.rationale: Populists accept popular sovereignty and majority rule, unlike extremists who reject democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Populism favors direct decisions such as referendums, and the Omaha Platform endorsed initiative and referendum.

right-to-secede.rationale: Some outsider movements favor regional independence and others defend the nation; the stance does not decide.

natural-rulers.rationale: Populism claims no elite has superior standing to rule and the people are the moral source of authority; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Strands differ from nonviolent protest movements to radical groups.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is a host-ideology matter, with secular left strands and religious right strands both anti-establishment.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Some right-wing strands want religious law while others do not, so the stance gives no answer.

military-superiority.rationale: Right strands favor it, 1960s strands opposed Cold War military spending.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Right-wing nativist hosts say yes and left strands no.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Left strands only; populism frames the divide as people versus elite rather than class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Left strands lean toward equality of outcome, right-wing strands do not; the stance is silent.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Handing decisions to technocratic systems moves power further from ordinary people; inferred from the people-versus-expert framing.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Fits distrust of state power over citizens; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Right strands seek restoration while 1960s strands wanted change.

direct-action.rationale: Anti-establishment movements are associated with street protest such as 1968, Seattle and Occupy, though populists also use elections.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Left strands such as Occupy might agree and right strands would not.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not part of the stance; populism speaks of the people as a collective.

conscription.rationale: Not part of the stance; Vietnam-era strands opposed it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Populism puts the popular vote and the people's general will at the center of legitimacy; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Right-wing anti-establishment strands see media and education as holding establishment power; left strands focus on finance, so contested.

total-state.rationale: Anti-establishment views oppose concentrated established power; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Hierarchical bondage contradicts the 'plain people' framing; anachronistic inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Both strands distrust institutional knowledge, but only parts of the left put it as theory.

universal-morality.rationale: Not part of the stance, though populism is moralistic.

single-common-good.rationale: Populism treats the people as homogeneous with one general will rather than balancing interests; inferred from Mudde's definition.

workplace-democracy.rationale: A left-strand idea that right-wing anti-establishment strands do not share.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding follows the host ideology, not the anti-elite stance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy follows the host ideology; both austerity critics and deficit hawks use anti-elite language.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian-leaning strands agree and left strands do not; the stance is silent.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not part of the stance; right strands favor it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Populism often prefers common sense over expertise but takes no side on faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Right-wing strands favor it, left strands do not.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Right-wing strands favor work conditions and left strands oppose them, so no stance-based answer follows.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social-conservative strands accept it and counterculture and liberation strands rejected it.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of the stance; the Omaha Platform's money plank dealt with currency, not a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: 1960s strands opposed it and contemporary mainstream strands reject it; no source states a position for the stance.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Left strands agree; populism sees elites rather than class dominating.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Right strands favor it; left strands do not.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Right strands favor it, left strands do not.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some right-wing strands hold it but it is outside the stance's core and fringe for most adherents.

proportional-representation.rationale: No stated position, though outsider parties often favor it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Left strands agree and right strands do not.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Corruption of and distance between the political class and ordinary people is the defining claim; the Omaha Platform says corruption dominates the ballot box and legislatures.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the stance; coercive state control over families is inconsistent with the stance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Left strands favor it, right strands defend security forces.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the stance; mainstream strands reject it, inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Populism claims to speak for ordinary people against a privileged elite, which fits equal standing, though some strands exclude out-groups.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strands differ by host ideology; the stance gives no answer.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Populism makes the general will of the people the goal of politics, so authority rests on popular consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Not part of the stance and inconsistent with mainstream populism, which accepts democratic limits, but some right strands differ.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Outsider movements are often the target of such bans, and populism distrusts institutions defining who may take part; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not part of the stance, though arbitrary elite power is the target.

separated-powers.rationale: Populists often accuse courts and media of being detached from the people, but the Omaha Platform sought checks through direct election of senators.

vanguard-party.rationale: Populism puts the people's will first rather than a revolutionary elite; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left strands yes, right strands no.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not stated, though it fits the anti-elite logic and some outsider movements propose it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Populism distrusts concentrated power, though in office populists often expand executive power; contested and inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Anti-establishment movements want to resist official control of information; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not part of the stance; inferred from opposition to concentrated power.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Right strands favor it, left strands do not.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Fits the claim that political elites are detached from ordinary people; inferred, not a stated plank.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is a feature of the establishment parties that populists criticize; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational bodies are seen as remote elites, as in anti-EU parties; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by senior religious officials is an establishment form; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not part of the stance, though 1960s strands opposed the Vietnam War.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Counterculture and many outsider movements resist official cultural control; right strands may differ.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not part of the stance; populist leaders often seek long tenure but the stance opposes entrenched incumbents.

recall-officials.rationale: Fits direct accountability of the political class to the people; inferred from the direct-democracy emphasis.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: 1960s strands opposed Cold War spending and right strands are split on alliances.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Omaha Platform came from farmers but the modern stance has no rural doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Right-wing anti-establishment strands portray education and expert classes as detached from ordinary people.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not part of the stance, though it fits a people-over-experts view, so strands split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: 1960s counterculture rejected conformity, but right strands do not.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine about socialist states, not addressed by the stance.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Left strands may accept price controls and market-leaning strands would not; inferred with no stated position.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nationalist strands favor reunification, but the stance itself does not address borders.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Left strands such as Occupy favour debt forgiveness while right-wing anti-establishment parties are mixed; the stance itself does not settle it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left anti-establishment movements link political and economic change while right populists stress sovereignty; the shared core is silent.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Anti-establishment populists typically want to rewrite the settlement through direct popular decision-making (Omaha Platform's direct democracy demands, populism's popular sovereignty); inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Anti-establishment politics is hostile to elite rule and unaccountable power, so a trade of freedoms for growth is disfavoured; inferred, as some populist leaders have curbed freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Left strands endorse aid and right populists often oppose it as elite internationalism; no shared position.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed by the stance; the host ideology decides.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Populism and the Omaha Platform favour direct election and popular control over indirect selection by elites.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Populism distrusts unelected, expert-run institutions insulated from the people, and the Omaha Platform attacked the money power; adherents want elected government control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A territorial question the anti-elite stance does not settle; nationalist hosts say no and anti-war hosts say yes.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Left strands (Omaha Platform's public ownership of railroads) agree while right-wing strands defend property; the core is neutral.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Depends on host ideology; anti-establishment politics takes no position on the Soviet Union's character.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The stance defines no environmental position; left strands favour precaution and right strands often oppose it.

collective-defense.rationale: Left and right anti-establishment movements disagree on alliances such as NATO, so the stance does not settle it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The stance is silent on territorial disputes; adherents take positions from their host ideology.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Left strands favour curbing church power while right populists often ally with religious institutions; not settled by the stance.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Populists often favour a leader who takes sides, while others value a unifying figure; adherents split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Position comes from the host ideology: separatists and unionists both appear among anti-establishment movements.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy is favoured by some anti-establishment movements and opposed by others; the stance is silent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Populism rests on popular sovereignty and distrust of inherited elites; a divine-descent ruler is the ultimate establishment. Inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Flat taxes appear in right-populist programs while left anti-establishment movements favour progressive rates; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: The stance has no view on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Omaha Platform charges that rulers and legislatures are corrupt and should be held accountable; a ruler above the law runs against that, though strongman populists differ. Inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: The stance is silent on space policy; adherents are split between space enthusiasm and a priority on Earth problems.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Populism favours direct popular decision-making over entrenched elite bodies, so a blend that guarantees the few a role is disfavoured. Inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Right-populist movements often build leader cults while others reject them as establishment trappings; adherents split.

equal-parenting.rationale: The stance is silent on custody; adherents take positions from their host ideology.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anti-establishment politics is a stance; the answer depends on the host ideology.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Omaha Platform demands that land held by railroads and speculators be reclaimed for actual settlers.

refugee-return.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Left and right strands differ, so no common answer follows from hostility to the establishment.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to state-imposed morality in the counterculture and populist right alike.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from populist distrust of supranational elite projects such as the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Left and right strands differ, so no common answer follows.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Omaha Platform attacks monopolies and corporate power over markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from Occupy and populist anger at rescues of banks and elites with taxpayers' money.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wikipedia's account of populism notes hostility to courts and independent bodies that block the popular will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Left strands favour quotas and right strands oppose them, so it is split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Host ideologies differ: protectionist right and internationalist left strands both occur.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the Seattle protesters' demand for labor and environmental conditions on trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: A stance without a program on this issue; host ideologies differ.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Strands differ; most use electoral or protest means, with no common view.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from hostility to privileged elites and inherited standing.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The stance has no curricular position; left strands oppose national narratives and right strands favour them.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hostility to ruling elites and rule over ordinary people leans against tutelage; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Right-wing anti-establishment movements favour it and left counterculture opposes it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Strands conflict, with right populists opposing preferences and left movements supporting them.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Omaha Platform demanded a national currency issued by the general government only, though other strands do not share this.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Left strands expect collapse and right strands do not; the stance does not settle it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The stance has no position on foreign influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Anti-globalisation left and nationalist right both attack integration, but the stance itself is not a trade doctrine.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: No position follows from opposition to elites; it depends on the host ideology.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Host ideologies diverge and the stance is silent.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Populists distrust courts and entrenched limits on majorities, yet the Omaha Platform sought constitutional reforms; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A stance against elites rather than a program; takes no position on colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Omaha Platform pushed popular election of officials; inferred as favouring election over inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: No documented position; the stance defines no rule on minority consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Populist rhetoric holds that rulers betraying the people lose legitimacy; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Anti-establishment movements distrust both parliaments and monarchs as elite institutions; inferred as neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Depends on the attached ideology; no core position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Depends on the attached ideology; no core position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rejects elite paternalism in favour of ordinary people; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The stance is about mobilising against elites rather than withdrawing; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Counterculture and New Left strands hold that media and mass culture serve elites; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Casts elites as holding power through control of institutions, media and culture; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Varies by attached ideology (left yes, right populists often no).

native-born-offices.rationale: Right-wing populists often yes, left strands no; inferred as split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Populists distrust unelected establishment institutions such as the military as arbiters; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: A stance rather than a program; traditional strands support it and counterculture strands reject it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from hostility to credentialed experts and entrenched institutions, though it also opposes patronage.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Left and right strands split, with populists often protectionist and others unconcerned; the stance does not settle it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; positions follow the host ideology.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Omaha Platform and populists demand direct popular control through initiative, referendum and accountability of officials.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; left and right strands differ on pension design.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; the host ideology decides, and the Omaha Platform's land proposals were specific to its time.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from populist demands for elected bodies to hold power, though anti-establishment distrust of legislatures weakens this.

single-official-language.rationale: Right-wing strands favour it and left strands oppose it; the stance does not settle it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Populist nationalists favour restriction while other strands do not.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Left strands support the idea and right strands oppose it; the stance has no position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from 1960s counterculture and Occupy criticism of consumer society, though right-wing strands are indifferent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from distrust of the foreign-policy establishment and its covert operations, though not a defining issue.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the same distrust of great-power elites, though no source addresses it.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Omaha Platform charges that corporations and wealth have corrupted government, and the stance casts the economic as well as political elite as corrupt.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A stance rather than a program; there is no shared position on foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No shared position; the stance takes its views on population from the attached ideology.

residents-only-property.rationale: No shared position on property restrictions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic programs come from the attached ideology, so this is neutral.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: the stance distrusts elite-led foreign policy projects such as democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: contempt for the establishment and its laws, with direct action favoured.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: hostility to elite-run interventions and foreign entanglements.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic organisation is not part of the shared core.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Populism casts a corrupt elite as the enemy, and conspiracy thinking is common, but targeting an ethnic minority comes from particular right-wing strands, not the shared core.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Opposing the establishment says nothing about whether the state should recognise marriage; anarchist strands might abolish it while right-wing populists defend it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: opposing an unaccountable elite favours transparency, which Omaha-style reform programs endorse.

local-production.rationale: No shared position; localism appears in some strands only.

informal-organisation.rationale: Counterculture and Occupy used informal groups while populist movements use parties, so it is split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: populists oppose rule by remote international bodies, consistent with the answers to empower-international-orgs.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion's role depends on the attached ideology.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anti-elite stances usually reject submission to outside powers as well as domestic ones; inferred from the people-versus-elite frame.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The stance has no fiscal position; strands differ, with some regionalists wanting to keep revenue and others not.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Left strands like Occupy and the Omaha Platform lean to common ownership of key sectors while right strands defend property; the stance does not settle it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism and communism both appear among anti-establishment movements; the stance is silent.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Strands split on public versus private delivery; the Omaha Platform wanted public ownership but modern populists vary.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is not a defining issue; left strands are secular and right populists often defend religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Omaha Platform attacked corporate and financial power, and anti-establishment movements cast economic elites as corrupt; this is inferred, not a view on capitalism as a stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left strands would agree, right populists would not; the stance takes no side.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a defining issue; right populist strands may like it, others have no view.

treaties-binding.rationale: No documented position; strands differ on minority and indigenous claims.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Counterculture strands favoured communes but most modern populism seeks to capture existing states; split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Only some right-wing populist strands would agree; the stance as such is silent.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejecting the established order fits a third course, but each strand has its own host ideology; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The stance takes its positions from the attached ideology; this one is not addressed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Distrust of elite narratives feeds some conspiracy thinking, but the stance does not endorse denial; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the stance's counterculture and anti-state-coercion side, mixed with strands that disagree.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anti-establishment politics opposes elites and defends popular opposition; the Omaha Platform attacks the suppression of the people's voice.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; the stance opposes enforced conventional orthodoxy, inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; positions on empire depend on the attached ideology.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; the stance rejects the ruling order but not specifically on religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Preference for direct popular decision-making is the shared core, as in the Omaha Platform's initiative and referendum.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The stance's positions come from the attached ideology; not addressed.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; depends on the strand.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; depends on the strand.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Mudde's account of populism pits the people against the elite across left and right, so the stance cuts across the division.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed; depends on the strand.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the stance depends on the attached ideology.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Populism often rests authority in the people against elites; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a topic the stance addresses.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the stance's hostility to elites seen as pursuing wars for their own ends, as in the 1960s counterculture and Occupy.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The stance carries no view on national definition; it takes this from whatever ideology it attaches to.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the Omaha Platform's demand for direct popular rule, which opposes carving up the electorate into bloc-represented communities that entrench party and insider deals.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the stance's charge that insiders act in secret against the people, so open dealings are the natural demand.

premarital-sex.rationale: Counterculture strands accept it and right-wing populist strands often do not; the stance itself implies no position.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: hostility to establishment control makes adherents wary of state censorship, though some strands would use it against opponents.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic positions come from the attached ideology, so the stance itself implies no position.

missingStatements.rationale: The Omaha Platform charges that corruption dominates the ballot box and legislatures, and the stance holds that the political class serves insiders over the people.

notes: Anti-establishment is a stance whose meaning depends on who is the establishment, so strands answer differently. Wikipedia reports the term was mostly left-wing in 1968 and mostly right-wing populist in the 2010s. Expect the salience check to find few stated positions.
